notes: Identity independently checked against title, authors Daniel M. Oppenheimer and Benoît Monin, Judgment and Decision Making 4(5), August 2009, pp. 326–334, and printed DOI 10.1017/S1930297500001170. The supplied text is a full primary article PDF text parse with Methods, Results and references; no PDF path was supplied. Target correspondence is unresolved: Study 2a has three pairwise comparisons, reported collectively as t(47,48,57) = 1.94, 2.32, 2.65, p < .05, Cohen’s d = .56, .67, .69). Neither the generic retrospective gambler’s fallacy description nor page 329 identifies a particular pair. No effect is selected by list order, df, or numerical matching. The omnibus test is separately printed on p. 328 as F(2, 77) = 4.8, p < .05, Cohen’s f = .18; this does not uniquely identify the requested d comparison. Candidate full-study analytic sample is 80: the Method reports eighty participants and footnote 2 says all data points were included. It is not entered as the unidentified pairwise analytic N. No N is derived from df; no effect size is converted. Unassigned p, replication, and success fields are placeholders.
